title: Three Terms and One Short Sandpit
subtitle: 学校教育 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 学校教育（人与自我·生活与学习·个人、家庭、社区及学校生活）
meta: 主题语境：学校教育（人与自我·生活与学习·个人、家庭、社区及学校生活）　|　核心词汇：kindergarten　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 kindergarten 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1992 the assistant ① opened the kindergarten that no neighbour in the room would have recorded, and he said the opening was the whole of the term. The ② kindergarten, meaning the school itself and not the sandpit, ran three terms and stayed unrecorded in the book; a kindergarten, he said, is the only thing in a room that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ kindergarten in that room had the same short sandpit beside it, and the ④ kindergarten at the far door, meaning the class they kept for the children to join and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A kindergarten, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the assistant said the recording is the part that fills three terms.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the kindergarten was the whole of the matter, meaning the start and not the school. The ⑥ kindergarten, meaning the start and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; kindergarten, he said, is either something you open or the only word that means both a school and a start. He said the start is the part they remember.

By 1997 the ⑦ kindergarten had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short sandpit. The ⑧ kindergarten of the whole thing, the assistant wrote in March, was one room and three terms of recording; kindergarten, he said, is either the class at the far door or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ kindergarten I remember is the school recorded in the plan, which closed in 1999 and is still recorded as the quietest in the room. A ⑩ kindergarten, my mother said in 2001, is the only school that improves by being recorded; every kindergarten, she said, is a start that has agreed to look like a school. She said the start was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 幼儿园（指活动室里每一所旁边的那一所）
B. n. 幼儿园（指那所园所本身，与沙坑相对）
C. 固定搭配：open the kindergarten 开办这所幼儿园
D. n. 幼儿园（指留给孩子们加入的一班那一所）
E. n. 启蒙之事（抽象总称，指一处活动室的幼儿园之事）
F. n. 幼儿园（指计划里写到、被记下的的那一所）
G. n. 起点、启蒙（指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 启蒙（抽象总称，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: opened the kindergarten that no neighbour in the room would have recorded
The kindergarten, meaning the school itself and not the sandpit
the kindergarten at the far door
the kindergarten was the whole of the matter
the kindergarten had become a line in a plan
The kindergarten of the whole thing
A kindergarten, my mother said in 2001

answers.why: open the kindergarten 意为“开办这所幼儿园”，1992 年那位助教把活动室里没有一位邻居肯记录的一所幼儿园做了一遍。
kindergarten 意为“幼儿园”，指那所园所本身而不是沙坑，它经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被记录。
kindergarten 意为“幼儿园”，指活动室里每一所旁边的那一所，每一所旁边都有同一个小小的沙坑。
kindergarten 意为“幼儿园”，指最远那扇门口留给孩子们加入的一班那一所，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
kindergarten 意为“起点、启蒙”，指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个起点就是那件事的全部。
kindergarten 意为“启蒙”，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西而不是那所园所，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
kindergarten 意为“幼儿园”，指计划里写到、被记下的的那一所，到 1997 年这一所成了计划里的一行。
kindergarten 意为“启蒙之事”，助教三月写道，整件事的幼儿园之事是一处活动室和三个学期的记录。
kindergarten 意为“幼儿园”，我记得的是计划里记录过的那一所，1999 年开园了，至今仍被说成活动室里最安静的一所。
kindergarten 为抽象总称，母亲 2001 年说，幼儿园是唯一会因为被好好记录而变得更好的园所。
